I have been farming my whole life, and I know my 3.5 mu in Quzhou like the back of my hand. With four people under my roof, I need grain first and cash second, so I split my land carefully. Three mu goes to my wheat-maize rotation — that is our food security. The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn; it is improved seed that does not lodge easily. Now that spring is starting, I will topdress it with urea when it greens up, and irrigate three times from my well: at green-up, at jointing, and at grain filling. I will spray twice for weeds and for the rust that comes when it turns humid. After cutting the wheat in early June, I will rotary till fast and plant hybrid maize the same day — summer is short here, and every day counts. The maize gets compound fertilizer at planting and a side-dressing of urea at the big trumpet stage; I will irrigate twice if the July heat dries things out, and spray twice for weeds and corn borer. The other half mu I keep for cotton because the cash buys school supplies and medicine. I plough that plot deep in spring, plant improved cotton seed, and give it extra potash because cotton needs that. Cotton bollworms are stubborn, so I will spray four times, and irrigate three times when it flowers and bolls. My well pump runs on electricity, so I only water when the crops truly need it — wasting water is wasting money. I expect about 500 kg per mu of wheat, 600 kg per mu of maize, and 280 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather cooperates.
